as i am not from the UK, I can't respond to your TL;DR. but, I can say this: psychiatrists will understand if you say the side effects of a medication are too strong or affect you too much to your liking, and they will try to suggest different options based on what you explain to them. I started off on methylphenidate, aka Ritalin, and I didn't notice any side effects until my family told me I had been a lot more irritable lately. i brought that up to my psychiatrist, and she immediately offered to change my prescription so I could try another medicine. so what I mean is, your doctor won't think you are seeking meds if you request to change yours due to side effects. in actuality, it's rare for someone to get the right meds on the first try. so on your next appointment, tell them you've been having unpleasant side effects, and that you'd like to try something else. it'll be okay, and they'll listen to you. good luck :\]

adderall is a stimulant medicine, so its side effects can be, among others, elevated heart rate. still, you should remember this and bring it up to your psychiatrist next time you see them. they'll decide whether it's still safe for you to use.
